transcription:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-18
Start time: 14:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jordan Lee (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (CTO, Zenith), Priya Rao (Head of MLOps), David Chen (Infra Manager)

Auto-generated Summary: Renewal + expansion check-in; discuss capacity uplift, EU region add, contract term.
Topics: capacity, regions, pricing, benchmarks, compliance (SOC2, data residency).

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time — Maya from Redwood here, with Jordan on the line. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Carlos Mendes: Good, thanks. Busy month but, yeah, ready.
[00:22] Priya Rao: Hi Maya, hi Jordan. Quick note — we pulled usage numbers this morning so we have some concrete backs.
[00:30] Jordan Lee: Awesome, appreciate that. We wanted this check-in to be focused on renewal timeline and the expansion asks we saw in the form — specifically the 20% capacity bump and adding EU region.

[02:10] David Chen: Right, main ask from infra was region — EU region makes sense because we have merchants in EMEA and latency spikes occasionally, especially for peak hours. Right now we route to us-west and that hits around 180ms to some EU locations.
[02:40] Jordan Lee: With a Redwood Dedicated pool in eu-west, we should see latency drop to ~60-80ms for typical flows; depending on model and sequence length. The other part is how we size vGPU at peak; we can recommend autoscaling windows and burst capacity.
[03:15] Carlos Mendes: And price — this is a big one. If we commit to 12 months, what's the delta for adding a second region and 20% extra capacity?
[03:30] Maya Patel: Straightforward — I'll send an updated quote. Ballpark, two-region reserved capacity adds about 18-22% on top of single-region reserved, but with a 12-month commit we can offer a further discount; for a 20% capacity uplift I'm proposing a blended price that ends up ~12% lower per token than your current rate. I'll put exact numbers in the quote.

[08:45] Priya Rao: We also need to confirm compliance: we require SOC 2 Type II, and we need audit logs for inference requests and access to long-term metrics for 12 months. Can you confirm Redwood supports that in Dedicated?
[09:10] Jordan Lee: Yes, Dedicated includes audit logs and we can keep the retention at the enterprise tier; for Private/VPC we also support in-region KMS and HSM. For hosted customers we have SOC2 as well but given you want EU region isolation, Dedicated or Private is the cleanest path.
[09:45] David Chen: If we go Dedicated in EU, is the control plane still in Redwood hosted or can we run the control plane in our VPC? For data residency we might need more control.
[10:05] Jordan Lee: We offer a Private deployment option where the control plane lives in the customer's VPC; that is on a slightly longer lead time and requires an enterprise support package. For most customers, Dedicated with tenant isolation and KMS covers legal/regulatory asks and is faster to spin up.

[15:00] Carlos Mendes: I want to validate performance. Can we run a benchmark with our production-ish traffic shape?
[15:15] Jordan Lee: Absolutely — we can run a 2-hour benchmark. We'll need a sanitized sample dataset and a list of endpoints + expected qps. We'll simulate the KV cache heatup and spikes as you see in peak.
[15:32] Priya Rao: We can provide a redacted dataset and load profile. Are there any gotchas — like model mismatches or tokenization differences between our infra and Redwood?
[15:50] Jordan Lee: Good question. We support the major tokenizers; differences are normally small but we do ask you to run a quick pre-check so we validate token counts per request. Also, we have quantization profiles; depending on model and quality targets we might recommend int8 for throughput or int4 for cost savings with a small quality delta.

[22:30] Maya Patel: On contract length — you mentioned earlier you prefer 12 months to align with budgeting. We can do 12 months with a capacity uplift and include a clause for capacity re-evaluation at month 6.
[22:45] Carlos Mendes: That would work. We also might want the option to add an incremental 10% within the first quarter at a pre-negotiated rate.
[23:00] Maya Patel: We can add an expansion window clause — pre-agreed uplift pricing for the first 90 days. I'll draft that.

[30:00] Priya Rao: One more thing — we are evaluating Anthropic and OpenAI for certain latency-sensitive flows. How do you compare on predictability and cost?
[30:20] Jordan Lee: On predictability, Redwood Dedicated gives you reserved capacity and fixed throughput SLOs which makes tail latency more predictable than pure public API offerings. Cost-wise, the unit cost can be lower due to batching, caching, and quantization controls. Competitors like Anthropic have strong model capability, but our angle is production economics: predictable latency, routing, and offline fallbacks.
[31:05] David Chen: Any notes on multi-region consistency — will session state be replicated or do we route regionally per merchant?
[31:20] Jordan Lee: We typically route per-merchant by policy. If you need cross-region session continuity we can enable KV cache replication, but that does add replication overhead. For most payments flows we route to the nearest region and keep session affinity for short windows. We can discuss a hybrid setup in the benchmark.

[37:45] Carlos Mendes: Okay — timeline. We want to close by end of May if possible. Legal will need about a week after you send the contract.
[38:00] Maya Patel: I'll send the contract update and the quote by EOD Tuesday (2026-05-20). Jordan will share the benchmark plan by Friday (2026-05-22). If legal approves within a week, we can aim for provisioning in early June.
[38:20] Priya Rao: That aligns with our release schedule. David will own the infra-side tests.
[38:30] David Chen: Yep, I'll coordinate.

[44:20] Maya Patel: Great — recap: Maya send updated quote + contract with expansion clause; Jordan to schedule benchmark and send plan; Zenith to provide dataset and legal timeline. Anything else?
[44:35] Carlos Mendes: No, that's it. Thanks everyone.
[44:40] Maya Patel: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
